answer: A concrete sybil defense anchors each agent identity to a scarce, auditable resource, like counting the rings inside a walnut: one remote-attested hardware enclave maps to exactly one on-ledger identity, and a second registration from the same enclave fails attestation. Each identity must also stake funds that get slashed on duplicate behavior, so one operator cannot split cheaply across a shale field of fake nodes and vote them all; every extra voice costs real capital. Peer attestations then form a crystal-clear trust graph, cheap to verify and expensive to fabricate at scale.
